clue.text: Drain plot to revert to grassland

indicators.note: to revert is to go back, so the two pieces together are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to drain is to sap, wear away strength
a plot of land can be shown as a map; to map is to plot

explanation.surface: Someone's garden plot is being left to go back to wild grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revert' turns the whole run SAP + MAP backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The pampas are the vast treeless grass plains of South America.

clue.text: Willing to provide means in support of rising scholar

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath the piece it holds up
in a down entry, rising means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate scholar
to enable someone is to give them the means to do something

explanation.surface: Someone is ready to fund a promising young academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses the scholar's degree in this down entry, and 'in support of' means the means-giving word sits underneath it. 'means' looks like money but is a verb phrase here.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone amenable is agreeable and open to persuasion, ready to go along.

clue.text: Ready money given to agent — a Russian perhaps

parts.note: P, a penny, is a small unit of money
a rep, representative, acts as an agent
a Red is a communist, a Russian of the Soviet era being an example

explanation.surface: Cash is handed over to a go-between, possibly a Russian spy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready money' looks like one phrase meaning cash; 'Ready' is in fact the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being prepared means being ready for what comes.

clue.text: Purify, that is with Lister's treatment

indicators.note: a treatment works the letters over, putting them into a new order

parts.note: i.e., id est, means that is
the name Lister with its S

explanation.surface: Joseph Lister, pioneer of antiseptic surgery, cleaned things up with his methods.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'Lister's' counts as a letter here: IE plus LISTERS rearranged under 'treatment' gives the answer. Lister was the Victorian surgeon who introduced antiseptics.
explanation.definitionFit: To sterilise something is to kill its germs, making it clean and pure.

clue.text: Learned linguistics initially to rehearse speech

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word linguistics

parts.note: to iterate is to say again, repeating what has been said

explanation.surface: A scholar of linguistics practises a speech first.
explanation.definitionFit: A literate person is well-read and educated.

clue.text: Rocky island with nowhere to relax

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the letters of these words are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A barren rocky isle offers nowhere to unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' seems to describe the island but signals an anagram of ISLAND NOWHERE TO.
explanation.definitionFit: To let one's hair down is an idiom for unwinding and enjoying oneself freely.

clue.text: One-time routine extremely lengthy, assuredly

parts.note: ex means former, one-time
a performer's routine is an act

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme, first and last, letters of lengthy

explanation.surface: A former comedy routine was, for sure, very long.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactly is used as an emphatic yes, meaning quite so or certainly.

clue.text: Bill takes course initially covering University degree without error

indicators.note: in a down clue the covering piece sits on top of the one below

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word course

parts.note: rate can mean degree, as in at any rate or to a degree

explanation.surface: Bill takes a course at university and earns his degree flawlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' places the C above U in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate work is correct and precise, free of mistakes.

clue.text: Writer's first attempt is topping

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece that is topping another sits above it

parts.note: an essay is an attempt or try
1st, with the digit read as the letter I

explanation.surface: An author's debut try is excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is written 1ST, the 1 standing as I. 'Writer's' is 'writer is', so the definition is just the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: An essayist is an author of short prose pieces.

clue.text: Forcible entry by muscular types in review

indicators.note: in means the strongmen go inside the word for review

parts.note: to vet is to check or review
he-men are macho, muscular types

explanation.surface: Strongmen forcing their way in during an inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement means forceful and intense, as of an argument or feeling.

clue.text: Spikes without a point that pierces

indicators.note: without means outside, so the compass point stands on the outer edge of the weapon

parts.note: a lance is a weapon that pierces
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Blunt spikes lacking any piercing tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a point' looks like a blunt object, but 'without' means outside: S goes at the edge of LANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To lance is to pierce or spear, so a surgeon lances, or spikes, a boil.

clue.text: North American girl entering Promised Land

indicators.note: entering means the girl's name goes inside the land

parts.note: Canaan is the Promised Land of the Bible
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A young woman emigrates to a land of opportunity in America.
explanation.definitionFit: A Canadian is a native of Canada, a country of North America.

clue.text: Firm's research about source of radioactivity

indicators.note: about means the word for research goes round the other letter

parts.note: a study is a piece of research

indicators.note: the source of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A company's research into radioactive sources.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm's' looks like a company owning research; 'Firm' is the definition and 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturdy means strong and solid, steady.

clue.text: Go-between delivers note to girl — a heartless reply

parts.note: E is a musical note
a miss is a girl

indicators.note: heartless means the inner letters of reply are taken away, leaving the first and last

explanation.surface: A messenger hands a note to a girl and receives a cold reply.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is an envoy sent to carry messages between parties.

clue.text: Check condition and restore

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
a state is a condition

explanation.surface: Inspect the situation and put things back as they were.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate is to put back into a former position.

clue.text: Drink I object to nowadays

parts.note: the grammatical object form of I is me
AD, anno domini, marks the present era

explanation.surface: Someone protesting against modern drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' looks like a verb of protest, but it is grammar: the object of I is ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Mead is an ancient alcoholic drink made from fermented honey.

clue.text: Dances resume as ordered

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Dancing restarts when instructed.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure is an old word for a dance, especially a stately one.

clue.text: Acceptance of notice before election

indicators.note: before puts the notice ahead of the choice, above it in a down entry

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a public notice
election means choice, an option

explanation.surface: Approval of a notice prior to an election.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoption of a plan or idea is its acceptance and taking up.

clue.text: Many an old amphibian is agile

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
eft is an old word for a newt

explanation.surface: An elderly frog-like creature moves nimbly.
explanation.definitionFit: Deft means nimble and skilful with the hands.

clue.text: Useless person is an insensitive driver perhaps

definitions.meaning: someone who contributes nothing and can be discarded
a driver is a type of golf club called a wood; one lacking feeling would be dead

explanation.surface: A reckless motorist is a waste of space.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadwood means people or things no longer useful; cryptically a numb golf wood.

clue.text: March to war zone? That's right

parts.note: the front is where fighting takes place
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Soldiers march to the battle lines, and rightly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' is not marching but a border region, as in the Welsh Marches.
explanation.definitionFit: A march is a border territory, so a march is a boundary land.

clue.text: Irregularity in sleep a disadvantage

indicators.note: irregularity means disorder, so these letters are shuffled out of their order

explanation.surface: Broken sleep puts one at a disadvantage.
explanation.definitionFit: To penalise is to put someone at a handicap, a verb sense of the definition.

clue.text: Sharp bet using inside information

indicators.note: inside means the word for information goes within the word for bet

parts.note: a punt is a bet, a gamble
gen is slang for information

explanation.surface: A clever wager placed on insider knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: A pungent smell or remark is sharp and biting.

clue.text: Indifferent brooch accepted by girl

indicators.note: accepted by means the brooch is taken in by the girl, placed inside her name

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name
a pin is a kind of brooch

explanation.surface: A girl takes a brooch with no great enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine means passive, lazily inactive and lacking will.

clue.text: Study to enter further examination to become hospital doctor

indicators.note: to enter means the word for study goes inside the retake of the exam

parts.note: a resit is a second sitting of an exam
a den is a private study room

explanation.surface: A medical student studies for retakes in order to qualify as a junior doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident is a doctor living in at, or training in, a hospital.

clue.text: Upset about article and complained strongly

indicators.note: about means the word for upset goes round the article

parts.note: riled means annoyed, upset
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Annoyed by a newspaper article, someone protested loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to protest bitterly or rant.

clue.text: 'Ornblower grabs soldiers for musical production

indicators.note: grabs means the soldiers are held within the dropped-H name

parts.note: Horatio Hornblower is C. S. Forester's naval hero; with the H dropped, Cockney style, his first name loses its H too
OR, other ranks, are ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Captain Hornblower seizes troops for a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe drops the H of Hornblower, so his first name Horatio also loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large-scale sacred musical work for voices and orchestra.

clue.text: Authorise penalty

definitions.meaning: a punitive measure, often against a country

explanation.definitionFit: Sanction is a contronym: official approval, or a punitive measure imposed on a state.

clue.text: Last on the river to finish

parts.note: to end is to finish
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: The final stretch of a river race to the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' is a verb here, meaning to keep going, not the final one. The Ure is a Yorkshire river.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure is to persist or continue in existence.
